q: Under the 1998 ISO Common Policy Conditions, how much written notice must the insurer give the first Named Insured to cancel a commercial policy for nonpayment of premium?
explain: The 1998 edition of IL 00 17 requires at least 10 days' notice when the insurer cancels for nonpayment and 30 days for any other reason. State amendatory endorsements can change these periods.

q: The Common Policy Conditions form includes all of the following conditions EXCEPT:
choices: Examination of Your Books and Records
Transfer of Your Rights and Duties Under This Policy
explain: IL 00 17 has six conditions: Cancellation, Changes, Examination of Books and Records, Inspections and Surveys, Premiums, and Transfer of Rights and Duties. Vacancy is a loss condition in property coverage forms such as CP 00 10.

q: A business buys one policy made up of Common Policy Declarations, Common Policy Conditions, a Commercial Property Coverage Part and a Commercial General Liability Coverage Part. This policy is best described as a:
explain: A commercial package policy combines property and liability coverage parts under common declarations and common conditions. A policy with only one coverage part is monoline.
source: IRMI glossary 'commercial package policy'; ISO IL 00 17 11 98 preamble

q: An endorsement, such as Protective Safeguards, that modifies both the Commercial Property and the Farm coverage parts is called a(n):
explain: Interline (IL) forms apply across more than one coverage part. IL 04 15 states that it modifies both the Commercial Property and Farm coverage parts.

q: Supplementary Payments under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form include up to what amount for bail bonds required because of accidents or traffic law violations arising out of the use of a covered vehicle?
explain: The 2013 ISO CGL pays up to $250 for bail bonds, but the insurer does not have to furnish them. Supplementary payments do not reduce the limits.

q: Which statement about Supplementary Payments under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form is correct?
choices: They reduce the general aggregate limit
They include attorneys' fees taxed against the insured
They apply only under Coverage C – Medical Payments
They are paid in addition to the limits of insurance
explain: The 2013 form says these payments 'will not reduce the limits of insurance.' Court costs are covered, but attorneys' fees taxed against the insured are not. They apply to Coverages A and B.
source: ISO CG 00 01 04 13, Supplementary Payments 1.e, final para.

q: A customer slips in an insured's store and incurs medical bills. Under Coverage C – Medical Payments of the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, which statement is correct?
choices: Payment requires proof that the insured was negligent
Coverage C pays injured employees of the insured
Expenses must be incurred and reported within one year of the accident
Expenses must be incurred and reported within three years of the accident
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, Coverage C pays regardless of fault, but only for expenses incurred and reported within one year of the accident. Injuries to insureds, which include employees, are excluded.

q: The General Aggregate Limit of a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy applies to all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Premises and operations damages under Coverage A
Products-completed operations damages under Coverage A
Personal and advertising injury damages under Coverage B
explain: Products-completed operations BI/PD falls under the separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate Limit. Everything else counts toward the General Aggregate.

q: Which of the following is NOT a personal and advertising injury offense under a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy?
choices: Wrongful eviction from a room a person occupies
Oral or written publication of material that slanders a person
Bodily injury to a customer caused by a defective product
explain: Bodily injury from a product is Coverage A (BI/PD, products-completed operations), not a Coverage B offense. The other three are listed P&AI offenses.

q: During the policy period, the named insured under a 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy forms a new corporation in which it holds a majority interest. No other similar insurance is available. The new corporation qualifies as a Named Insured:
choices: Only after it is added by endorsement
Until the 30th day after it is formed or the policy period ends, whichever is earlier
Until the 90th day after it is formed or the policy period ends, whichever is earlier
For the rest of the policy period, even if more than 90 days remain
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, newly acquired or formed organizations (other than partnerships, joint ventures or LLCs) are automatic Named Insureds until the 90th day or policy expiration, whichever is earlier. There is no coverage for injury or offenses before the acquisition or formation.

q: An insured business borrows a 22-foot sailboat it does not own and takes clients out on it at no charge. A guest is injured. Under the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, the aircraft, auto or watercraft exclusion:
choices: Applies unless the boat was ashore on premises the insured owns or rents
Does not apply only if the clients paid a charge for the trip
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, exclusion g. has an exception for watercraft you do not own that are less than 26 feet long and not carrying persons or property for a charge.

q: Which of the following is NOT an insured contract under a Commercial General Liability (CGL) policy?
choices: The part of a premises lease that indemnifies the landlord for fire damage to the rented premises
An obligation required by ordinance to indemnify a municipality, other than in connection with work for the municipality
explain: A lease of premises is an insured contract, but the part that indemnifies for fire damage to rented premises is specifically carved out. That exposure is handled by the Damage To Premises Rented To You limit.

q: A contractor finishes one part of a project, and the owner starts using that part while other contractors keep working elsewhere on the project. Under a Commercial General Liability policy, an injury arising from the finished part is treated as:
choices: Ongoing operations until all work called for in the contract is finished
Completed operations only after the owner signs a written acceptance certificate
explain: Under CG 00 01's "products-completed operations hazard" definition, work is deemed completed at the earliest of: all work called for in the contract is done; all work at the job site is done, if the contract calls for work at more than one site; or that part of the work at a site is put to its intended use by anyone other than another contractor or subcontractor on the same project.

q: A business has a claims-made CGL policy from January 1, 2026, to January 1, 2027, with a retroactive date of January 1, 2022. It had no earlier claims-made policy, never reported an occurrence to the insurer, and did not buy the Supplemental Extended Reporting Period. Which claim is covered?
choices: Injury on June 1, 2021; claim first made March 1, 2026
Injury on June 1, 2023; claim first made March 1, 2026
Injury on August 1, 2026; claim first made February 1, 2028
Injury on March 1, 2027; claim first made May 1, 2027
explain: Coverage requires injury after the retroactive date and before the policy ends, and a claim first made during the policy period (or an ERP). The 2028 claim is more than 60 days after expiration, and the occurrence was never reported, so even the basic ERP does not apply.
source: FC&S 'Claims-Made CGL Form' (2014, CG 00 02 04 13); Austin & Stanovich, 'The Claims-Made CGL Policy' (2012)

q: Under the Basic Extended Reporting Period of a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy, a claim arising from an occurrence reported to the insurer within 60 days after the policy ended may be made up to:
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the automatic, no-charge basic ERP is 5 years for claims from occurrences reported within 60 days after the policy ends. It is only 60 days for claims from occurrences that were never reported.

q: Under a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy, the insured must request the Supplemental Extended Reporting Period in writing within how many days after the policy period ends, and the additional premium cannot exceed what percentage of the annual premium?
choices: Request within 30 days; premium no more than 100%
Request within 60 days; premium no more than 200%
Request within 60 days; premium no more than 300%
Request within 90 days; premium no more than 150%
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the supplemental ERP must be requested in writing within 60 days, costs no more than 200% of the annual premium, has unlimited duration, and reinstates the aggregate limits.

q: The insurer is not canceling or nonrenewing a 2013 ISO claims-made CGL policy. Within 60 days after the policy period ends, the first Named Insured asks in writing for claim and occurrence information. How soon after the request must the insurer provide it?
explain: Under the 2013 ISO claims-made CGL, the insurer provides the information within 45 days of the written request. If the insurer cancels or nonrenews, it must provide the information at least 30 days before termination.

q: A building owner requires its contractor to buy an Owners and Contractors Protective (OCP) policy for a project. Which statement about the OCP policy is correct?
choices: The owner is insured for the contractor's operations and its own general supervision of them
Coverage continues after the contractor's work has been completed and put to its intended use
The contractor is the named insured, and the owner is an additional insured
Any return premium is paid to the owner as the first Named Insured
explain: OCP insures the owner (the named insured) for BI/PD arising from the designated contractor's work at the specified location, or from the owner's general supervision. It excludes injury after the work is completed or put to its intended use, and premium refunds go to the 'contractor'.
source: ISO CG 00 09 04 13, Sec. I 1.b(1); Excl. 2.c; Sec. IV 2.e

q: Under the pollution exclusion of the 2013 ISO Commercial General Liability (CGL) Coverage Form, which of the following is still covered?
choices: Cleanup costs ordered by a state environmental agency
Bodily injury from pollutants at a waste disposal site the insured used
Bodily injury from heat, smoke or fumes from a hostile fire at the insured's premises
Property damage from chemicals the insured's subcontractor brought to an outdoor job site and spilled
explain: Under the 2013 ISO CGL, injury from a 'hostile fire' (one that becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be) is an exception to the premises pollution exclusion. Government-ordered cleanup costs and waste-site and job-site pollutants are excluded.

q: The 1988 ISO Commercial Property Conditions require a legal action against the insurer to be brought within:
choices: 1 year after the loss is reported to the insurer
2 years after the date of the direct physical loss
3 years after the policy period expires
5 years after the date of the direct physical loss
explain: The 1988 CP 00 90 requires full compliance with the coverage part and suit within 2 years after the direct physical loss occurred. Inland marine (CM 00 01) instead runs 2 years from when the insured first has knowledge of the loss.
source: ISO CP 00 90 07 88, D.; CM 00 01 09 04, Gen. Cond. C

q: A building insured by its owner under the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form has been vacant for 75 consecutive days when a windstorm, a covered cause of loss, damages it. How is the loss handled?
choices: Covered, but the payment is reduced by 15%
Covered, but the payment is reduced by 50%
explain: Under the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, after more than 60 consecutive days of vacancy, vandalism, sprinkler leakage, building glass breakage, water damage, theft and attempted theft are not covered. Other covered losses, such as windstorm, are reduced by 15%.

q: A building valued at $500,000 at the time of loss is insured for $300,000 under the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form with 80% coinsurance and a $1,000 deductible. A $100,000 covered loss occurs. How much does the insurer pay?
explain: Under the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, required insurance is $500,000 × 80% = $400,000. $300,000 ÷ $400,000 = 0.75, and $100,000 × 0.75 = $75,000. Subtract the $1,000 deductible: $74,000.

sub: Building and Personal Property – Coverage Extensions
q: Which coverage extension in the 2012 ISO Building and Personal Property Coverage Form is correctly matched with its limit?
choices: Personal effects and property of others – $10,000 per premises
explain: In the 2012 edition of CP 00 10, the correct limits are: newly acquired buildings $250,000 (BPP $100,000), property off-premises $10,000, outdoor property $1,000 with $250 per tree, shrub or plant, and personal effects and property of others $2,500.

q: In the 2012 ISO Business Income (and Extra Expense) Coverage Form, the period of restoration for Business Income coverage begins:
choices: Immediately after the direct physical loss
24 hours after the direct physical loss
72 hours after the direct physical loss
explain: Under the 2012 form, for Business Income the period of restoration starts 72 hours after the direct physical loss. For Extra Expense it starts immediately.

q: A bank has a $100,000 limit and loss payment percentages of 40%–80%–100% under the 2012 ISO Extra Expense Coverage Form. After a fire, its period of restoration is 45 days and it incurs $90,000 of extra expense. The insurer pays:
explain: Under the 2012 form, for a period of restoration of 31–60 days, the second percentage (80%) applies: $100,000 × 80% = $80,000. The remaining $10,000 is not covered.

q: Under the Condominium Commercial Unit-Owners Coverage Form, if the condominium association has other insurance covering the same property, the unit-owner's coverage is:
choices: Primary, with the association's insurance as excess
Shared pro rata by limits with the association's insurance
Shared equally with the association's insurance
explain: CP 00 18 is intended to be excess over the association's insurance. The association form (CP 00 17) is intended to be primary and waives subrogation against unit-owners.

q: Unless the insurer specifies otherwise in writing, coverage under the 1995 ISO Builders Risk Coverage Form ends no later than how long after construction is complete?
explain: Under the 1995 form, coverage ceases at the earliest of several events, including 90 days after construction is complete or 60 days after the building is occupied in whole or in part or put to its intended use.

q: Which peril is covered by the Causes of Loss – Broad Form but not by the Causes of Loss – Basic Form?
choices: Weight of snow, ice or sleet
explain: Broad adds falling objects; weight of snow, ice or sleet; and water damage, plus an Additional Coverage for collapse. Sprinkler leakage and sinkhole collapse are already Basic perils, and theft is not a covered peril in either form.

q: Under the 2017 ISO Causes of Loss – Special Form, the special theft limit for stamps, tickets and letters of credit is:
explain: In the 2017 Special Form, the special theft limits are $2,500 for furs, $2,500 for jewelry and watches, $2,500 for patterns, dies, molds and forms, and $250 for stamps, tickets and letters of credit.

q: Coverage B of the Ordinance or Law Coverage endorsement pays for:
choices: The loss in value of the undamaged portion of the building
The cost to demolish undamaged parts and clear the site
The increased cost to repair or rebuild the building to code
The loss of business income during demolition
explain: Coverage A is loss to the undamaged portion, Coverage B is demolition cost, and Coverage C is increased cost of construction.

q: A toy retailer's inventory roughly doubles from October through December each year. Which commercial property endorsement raises the personal property limit only during scheduled periods?
explain: CP 12 30 increases the limit on covered personal property by a scheduled amount at the described locations, only during the scheduled dates.

q: A store clerk is threatened with a gun and forced to hand over merchandise. Under ISO commercial crime definitions, this is:
explain: Robbery is the unlawful taking of property from a person's care and custody by someone who caused or threatened bodily harm, or committed an obviously unlawful act witnessed by that person. Burglary involves unlawful entry or exit from premises.
source: ISO CR 00 21 11 15, F. def. 20; IRMI glossary 'burglary'

sub: Commercial Crime – Loss Sustained vs Discovery
q: Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form (Loss Sustained Form), loss sustained before cancellation is covered if discovered no later than how long after cancellation, unless replacement insurance takes effect first?
explain: Under the 2015 Loss Sustained Form, the extended period to discover loss is one year, but it ends immediately when other replacement insurance takes effect.

sub: Commercial Crime – Loss Sustained vs Discovery
q: Which statement best describes the Commercial Crime Coverage Form (Discovery Form)?
choices: It covers loss discovered during the policy period, no matter when it occurred
It covers only losses that both occur and are discovered during the policy period
It covers occurrences during the policy period discovered up to 1 year after cancellation
It covers only employee theft, not robbery or burglary by outsiders
explain: The discovery form is triggered by discovery, and the occurrence can be at any time. It allows a 60-day period to discover loss after the policy ends. The 1-year tail belongs to the loss sustained form.
source: Rough Notes PF&M 251.4-2 (ISO crime forms analysis); ISO CR 00 21 11 15, E.1.g

q: Under the 2015 ISO Commercial Crime Coverage Form, which loss is covered by the Inside the Premises – Theft of Money and Securities insuring agreement?
choices: Unexplained disappearance of money from the premises
Theft of merchandise from the sales floor by a burglar
Embezzlement of cash from the register by an employee
Counterfeit bills accepted in good faith in a sale
explain: In the 2015 form, this agreement covers money and securities inside the premises (or a financial institution's premises) against theft, disappearance or destruction. Merchandise is 'other property', covered only for robbery of a custodian or safe burglary (Insuring Agreement 4); ordinary burglary of merchandise from the sales floor is not covered. Employee embezzlement falls under Employee Theft, and counterfeit bills under Money Orders and Counterfeit Money.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the classes in the Nationwide Marine Definition?
explain: The classes are imports; exports; domestic shipments; bridges, tunnels and other instrumentalities of transportation and communication; personal property floaters; and commercial property floaters. Buildings and their contents are not marine risks (MCL 500.614 excludes them).

q: Under the 2004 ISO Commercial Inland Marine Conditions form, which statement is correct?
choices: The insured may abandon damaged property to the insurer for full payment
Each claim payment reduces the limit of insurance for the remainder of the policy period
Legal action must be brought within 1 year of the loss
Claim payments do not reduce the limit, except for the total loss of a scheduled item
explain: The 2004 edition of CM 00 01 has a Reinstatement of Limit After Loss condition. It also prohibits abandonment and allows legal action within 2 years after the insured first has knowledge of the loss.
source: ISO CM 00 01 09 04, Loss Cond. A, I; Gen. Cond. C

q: Which inland marine class is an ISO filed class rather than a nonfiled class?
explain: Verisk lists accounts receivable among its filed classes, along with valuable papers, commercial articles, equipment dealers, signs and others. Contractors equipment, motor truck cargo and installation are nonfiled.

q: A common carrier is generally liable for loss of cargo in its care unless the loss is caused by:
explain: Common carriers are liable for cargo loss except loss caused by an act of God, the public enemy, an act of the shipper, public authority, or the inherent vice of the goods. The carrier must also prove it was not negligent.
source: Missouri Pacific R.R. v. Elmore & Stahl, 377 U.S. 134 (1964)

q: The Equipment Breakdown Protection Coverage Form values covered property on a replacement cost basis unless:
choices: The insured has fewer than 10 employees
The insured fails to meet a coinsurance requirement
The equipment is more than 20 years old
An Actual Cash Value endorsement is attached
explain: Replacement cost is built into the basic equipment breakdown form. Attaching the Actual Cash Value endorsement (often used for older equipment) changes the valuation to actual cash value.
source: FC&S 'Equipment Breakdown Coverage Form' (propertycasualty360.com, 2016); FC&S 'Equipment Breakdown Endorsements' (2018)

q: In the ISO farm property program, Coverage E applies to:
explain: A = Dwellings, B = Other Private Structures, C = Household Personal Property, D = Loss of Use, E = Scheduled Farm Personal Property, F = Unscheduled Farm Personal Property, G = Other Farm Structures. Edition note: these letters are from FP 00 10 09 94.

q: In the Farm Liability Coverage Form, Coverage J is:
choices: Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
explain: Coverage H is BI/PD liability, Coverage I is personal and advertising injury, and Coverage J is medical payments (expenses incurred or ascertained within 3 years of the accident).

q: A tenant wants coverage for its legal liability for damage to the landlord's building it occupies, caused by a covered cause of loss. Which commercial property coverage form is designed for this?
explain: CP 00 40 pays sums the insured is legally obligated to pay for direct physical loss to tangible property of others in its care, custody or control, caused by accident and arising from a covered cause of loss. It includes defense.

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, Business Income covers loss during a period of restoration that occurs within what time after the direct physical loss, and how is it limited?
choices: 6 consecutive months; subject to the building limit
12 consecutive months; not subject to the Section I limits
12 consecutive months; limited to 25% of the Business Personal Property limit
18 consecutive months; subject to a separate declared limit
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, Business Income is an Additional Coverage paying actual loss sustained for up to 12 consecutive months, with no dollar limit (it is not subject to the Section I limits). Ordinary payroll is limited to 60 days unless more days are shown.

q: After operations resume, Extended Business Income under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form lasts until income is restored or up to how many consecutive days, unless the Declarations show more?
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, Extended Business Income lasts up to 60 consecutive days after the date property is repaired and operations resume.

q: A building with a full replacement cost of $400,000 is insured for $240,000 under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form. A partial loss costs $50,000 to repair; its actual cash value is $30,000. The insured promptly repairs the building. Ignoring the deductible, the insurer pays:
explain: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, the limit is below 80% of replacement cost ($320,000), so the BOP pays the greater of ACV ($30,000) or ($240,000 ÷ $320,000) × $50,000 = $37,500. The BOP has no coinsurance clause, but this 80% rule applies to replacement cost recovery.

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Business Personal Property limit automatically increases by 25%, or by another percentage shown in the Declarations, for seasonal variations, but only if:
choices: The insured reports the values of its business personal property to the insurer by the end of each month
The loss occurs between November 1 and January 31
The insured is a retail store whose stock rises during a peak season shown in the Declarations
The limit is at least 100% of average monthly values for the prior 12 months or time in business, if less
explain: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners form, the seasonal increase applies only if the BPP limit is at least 100% of the average monthly values for the lesser of the preceding 12 months or the time in business.

q: Which additional coverage in the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form is correctly matched with its standard limit?
explain: The 2013 ISO Businessowners limits are Money Orders and Counterfeit Money $1,000, Forgery or Alteration $2,500, Electronic Data $10,000 per policy year, and Fire Extinguisher Systems Recharge $5,000.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.j, k, o, p

q: In the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Fire Department Service Charge additional coverage pays up to what amount per premises, unless the Declarations show a different limit?
explain: The 2013 ISO BOP pays up to $2,500 per premises with no deductible. The commercial property BPP form (CP 00 10) pays $1,000.
source: ISO BP 00 03 07 13, Sec. I A.5.c, D.3

q: Under the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the Newly Acquired or Constructed Property extension covers each building up to what limit, and for how many days after acquisition or start of construction, unless values are reported sooner?
explain: In the 2013 ISO BOP, the extension covers buildings up to $250,000 each and business personal property up to $100,000 per building. Coverage ends at policy expiration, 30 days after acquisition or start of construction, or when values are reported.

q: Under ISO businessowners program rules, which business is ineligible for a Businessowners policy regardless of its size?
explain: Per IRMI's summary of ISO rules, bars and pubs, auto repair and dealers, manufacturers, places of amusement, and banks are ineligible regardless of size. Apartments, offices and mercantile risks are eligible classes.

q: A Businessowners policy written on the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form shows a Liability and Medical Expenses limit of $1,000,000. The policy's products-completed operations aggregate limit is:
explain: Under the 2013 ISO BOP, both the products-completed operations aggregate and the general aggregate equal twice the Liability and Medical Expenses limit.

q: An accounting firm insured under a Businessowners policy is sued for an error in a client's tax return. Under Section II – Liability, the claim is:
choices: Covered as personal and advertising injury
Covered only if the error appeared in the firm's advertisement
explain: BP 00 03 excludes injury caused by rendering or failing to render any professional service, including legal and accounting services (and a client's purely financial loss is not bodily injury or property damage in the first place). This exposure needs E&O/professional liability coverage.

q: Under Section III – Common Policy Conditions of the 2013 ISO Businessowners Coverage Form, the insurer may cancel on as little as 5 days' written notice if:
choices: The building has been vacant or unoccupied 60 or more consecutive days
Premium has not been paid by the due date
The insured has filed two or more claims within the same policy year
The insured changes agents or moves its business to a new location
explain: In the 2013 ISO BOP, the 5-day cancellation applies to listed building conditions such as 60+ consecutive days of vacancy or unoccupancy (other than seasonal unoccupancy or construction, renovation or addition), repairs not started within 30 days of loss payment, or a vacate or demolition order. Nonpayment requires 10 days, and other reasons 30 days.

q: In the Protective Safeguards endorsement schedule, the symbol 'P-1' refers to:
choices: Service contract with a privately owned fire department
explain: P-1 is automatic sprinkler system, P-2 automatic fire alarm, P-3 security service, P-4 service contract with a private fire department, and P-9 a system described in the schedule.
source: ISO IL 04 15 04 98; FC&S 'Businessowners Program Endorsements Described' (2020, BP 04 30 07 13)

q: A Businessowners policy includes the Protective Safeguards endorsement, which lists an automatic fire alarm connected to a central station. The insured knows the alarm has been disconnected for weeks but does not tell the insurer. A fire then damages the building. The fire loss is:
choices: Covered for business personal property only
explain: The endorsement excludes fire loss if, before the fire, the insured knew of a suspension or impairment of a listed safeguard and failed to notify the insurer, or failed to keep it in complete working order.

q: A restaurant loses income when a fire at an off-premises power substation interrupts its electric service. Which Businessowners policy endorsement covers the lost income?
explain: Utility Services – Time Element (BP 04 57) covers Business Income and Extra Expense from interruption of utility service caused by covered damage to scheduled off-premises utility property. Direct Damage (BP 04 56) covers physical damage to covered property.

q: Under the Utility Services endorsements for a Businessowners policy, loss caused by damage to overhead transmission lines is:
choices: Covered whenever power supply property is indicated in the Schedule
Covered only if indicated in the Schedule
Covered only for water supply property
explain: Communication and power supply property do not include overhead transmission lines unless the Schedule indicates them.

sub: Selected Endorsements – Hired and Non-Owned Auto
q: An employee runs a business errand in her own car and causes an accident. The employer is sued. Which Businessowners policy endorsement or optional coverage covers the employer's liability?
choices: Hired Auto and Non-Owned Auto Liability
explain: BP 04 04 covers BI/PD from use of a non-owned auto in the insured's business by any person, and from use of hired autos. A premium must be shown in the Declarations.

q: When claims exhaust the aggregate limit of an underlying liability policy, an umbrella policy with a drop-down provision will:
choices: Suspend coverage until the underlying policy renews
Respond in place of the exhausted underlying coverage
Require the insured to buy a new underlying limit first
explain: One umbrella function is to drop down and pick up where the underlying policy leaves off when its aggregate is exhausted. Umbrellas also provide excess limits and cover some claims not covered by underlying policies, subject to a self-insured retention.
source: IRMI glossary 'umbrella liability policy'; 'drop down provision'

q: Under a directors and officers (D&O) liability policy, which insuring agreement reimburses the corporation for amounts it pays to indemnify its directors and officers?
explain: Side A covers directors and officers directly when the company can't or won't indemnify. Side B (corporate reimbursement) reimburses the company. Side C (entity coverage) covers the organization itself, typically for securities claims.
source: IRMI glossary 'Side A coverage', 'corporate reimbursement coverage', 'entity securities coverage'

q: The trustee of a company's 401(k) plan makes an imprudent investment choice. Plan participants sue for breach of fiduciary duty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Which coverage is designed to respond?
explain: Fiduciary liability covers errors in administering benefit plans under ERISA. The ERISA fidelity bond protects the plan only against fraud or dishonesty by people handling plan funds.

q: A former employee sues her employer alleging wrongful termination and sexual harassment. Which coverage is designed for this claim?
choices: CGL Coverage A – Bodily Injury and Property Damage Liability
explain: EPLI covers wrongful acts arising from the employment process (e.g., wrongful termination, harassment, discrimination). Workers compensation covers job-related injury and disease, and CGL Coverage A excludes bodily injury to employees.

q: Michigan law requires a retail liquor licensee to file proof of financial responsibility for dram shop liability of not less than:
explain: The proof may be liquor liability insurance, a surety bond, cash or securities, or a group self-insurance pool. A licensee may cancel liquor liability insurance only on 30 days' notice to the commission, with replacement proof.

q: In a construction performance bond, the project owner who is protected if the contractor fails to perform is the:
explain: The bond is executed by the principal (the contractor) and the surety to assure the principal's obligations to a third party, the obligee.

q: Which bond assures that a contractor will pay the persons who supply labor and material for the project?
explain: A payment bond assures payment to suppliers of labor and material. A performance bond secures completion of the contract. A bid bond assures the bidder will sign the contract and furnish the required bonds.

q: How does a surety bond differ from a typical insurance policy?
choices: The surety expects losses and prices the bond to pay them
The obligee pays the premium and indemnifies the surety
Only two parties are involved: the surety and the principal
The principal must reimburse the surety for losses it pays
explain: A surety bond is a three-party contract. The surety is secondarily liable and underwrites expecting no losses, and the principal must indemnify the surety for any loss it pays.
source: surety.org 'What is a Surety Bond?'; SFAA/AGC Surety Claims Guide

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, each surplus lines policy delivered to an insured must bear a notice, in red ink and at least 10-point type, stating that:
choices: The policy is protected by the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association if the insurer becomes insolvent and cannot pay claims
The insurer is not licensed by Michigan, and if it is insolvent, payment of claims may not be guaranteed
The rates and forms were approved by DIFS before the policy was issued
The agent is personally liable for claims if the insurer becomes insolvent
explain: MCL 500.1922 requires the notice: 'This insurance has been placed with an insurer that is not licensed by the state of Michigan. In case of insolvency, payment of claims may not be guaranteed.'

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, a surplus lines licensee must pay what tax and fee on surplus lines premiums written?
choices: 3% premium tax and no regulatory fee
explain: The licensee files sworn statements by February 15 and August 15 and pays the 2% premium tax plus a 0.5% regulatory fee.

q: Under Michigan's surplus lines law, coverage is presumed to be available from authorized insurers for all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Any coverage readily available from 3 or more authorized insurers at competitive terms
Michigan no-fault auto insurance for someone who is not a self-insurer
Coverage not obtainable after a diligent search among authorized insurers
explain: Coverage that cannot be procured after a diligent search among authorized insurers is presumed UNAVAILABLE and may be exported. The other three are presumed available.

q: Which statement about the Write Your Own (WYO) program of the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) is correct?
choices: Private insurers write and service policies in their own names; the federal government pays losses
Policies are sold and serviced by FEMA employees instead of private insurers
WYO companies set their own flood rates and policy forms, subject to state insurance department approval
WYO policies provide broader coverage than the same policy bought from NFIP Direct
explain: WYO companies are private P&C insurers that write and service NFIP policies in their own names, and the federal government pays all losses. Coverage is the same whether the policy comes from a WYO company or NFIP Direct.
source: FEMA brochure 'Meeting the Flood Insurance Requirement' (07-2024); agents.floodsmart.gov 'Flood Insurance 101'

q: A homeowner buys a National Flood Insurance Program flood policy at the closing of a new mortgage loan. What waiting period applies?
explain: The standard waiting period is 30 days, but there is none when coverage is bought in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan. Other exceptions apply after map revisions and for post-wildfire flooding.

q: What is the maximum building coverage available from the National Flood Insurance Program for a non-residential building?
explain: Non-residential maximums are $500,000 building and $500,000 contents. Single-family and 2-4 family residential buildings max out at $250,000 (residential contents $100,000); other residential buildings with 5 or more units can be insured up to $500,000.
source: 44 CFR 61.6(a); FEMA 'NFIP Summary of Coverage - Commercial Property' (01-2024)

q: Under the National Flood Insurance Program's Risk Rating 2.0 rules, what is the minimum building deductible for a residential building with more than $100,000 of building coverage and no pre-FIRM statutory discount?
explain: The minimum is $1,000 for building coverage of $100,000 or less and $1,250 for over $100,000. Pre-FIRM statutorily discounted buildings have $1,500/$2,000 minimums. Values as stated in FEMA guidance current in 2024–2025.
source: FEMA RR2.0 'Simple Guide for Residential Manufactured/Mobile Homes' (citing FIM Sec. 3)

q: Which statement about a risk retention group under the federal Liability Risk Retention Act is correct?
choices: It may write property and liability insurance for the general public
It must be licensed as an insurer in every state where it does business
It must participate in each state's insurance guaranty association
It is owned by its members and writes only liability insurance for them
explain: An RRG is chartered as a liability insurer in one state, owned by members in similar businesses, and limited to liability coverage. States may not require or permit it to join guaranty funds.

q: Which one of the following is a third-party cyber coverage?
choices: Payments to consumers whose data was exposed
Business income lost during a network outage
explain: Third-party coverage protects the insured from liability claims by others, such as affected consumers. Forensics, notification and business interruption are first-party costs.
